subtopics.title: The Timing Problem — Four New Adjustments

questions.question: The timing problem exists because:
options: Money moves on its own schedule, but matching demands each year carry exactly its own incomes and expenses
Banks close in June
The trial balance cannot handle cash
Expenses may only be recorded when paid

questions.question: The two-by-two grid is built from the two questions:
options: Is it big, and is it recurring?
Expense or income — and did the cash move before or after the use/earning it belongs to?
Debit or credit — and which journal?
Asset or liability — and which ledger?

questions.question: Income already received but not yet earned is called:
options: Accrued income
Prepaid income
Income received in advance
Deferred expense

questions.question: Every timing adjustment is always:
options: A cash entry in the CPJ
Two income-statement corrections
A note with no double entry
One income-statement correction PLUS one balance-sheet creation — the pair

subtopics.title: The Expense Side — Accrued and Prepaid

questions.question: Water and Electricity shows R2 640; June's R300 account arrives in July. The adjustment:
options: Debit Water and Electricity R300, credit Accrued Expenses (current liability) — the year used twelve months
Credit Water and Electricity R300 — only paid months count
Debit Bank R300
No entry until July

questions.question: Insurance of R1 800 was paid on 1 March for twelve months (year end 30 June). This year's true expense is:
options: R1 800 — it was all paid this year
R600 — four months used (March to June); the rest is next year's cover
Nothing — insurance is an asset

questions.question: The prepaid R1 200 becomes:
options: A current liability
Extra income
Prepaid Expenses — a CURRENT ASSET: value bought and stored for next year
A deduction from Capital

questions.question: What both expense cases share:
options: Both increase the bank balance
Both create liabilities
Both leave the expense at what was PAID
The expense ends at what the YEAR USED, regardless of what the bank account did

subtopics.title: The Income Side, plus the Interest That Joins the Loan

questions.question: The tenant (R600/month) has paid only eleven months by year end. Rent Income must be:
options: Credited R600 to the true R7 200, with Accrued Income debited as a current ASSET
Left at R6 600 — cash is cash
Debited R600
Closed off to the loan

questions.question: If instead the tenant paid THIRTEEN months, the extra R600 is:
options: Extra income for this year
Income received in advance — a current LIABILITY: the business owes a month of occupation
A donation
Accrued income

questions.question: "Interest capitalised" on the R15 000 loan at 10% means:
options: The interest was paid in cash monthly
The loan was repaid
The R1 500 interest was ADDED to the loan — expense debited, loan rising to R16 500
The interest was waived by the bank

questions.question: Missing the capitalised interest causes:
options: One error — profit only
No error — cash never moved
An overstated liability
TWO errors at once — the expense understated and the liability understated

subtopics.title: The Balance-Sheet Afterlives and Exam Technique

questions.question: The five afterlives, in order (accrued expense / prepaid expense / accrued income / income in advance / interest capitalised):
options: Current liability / current asset / current asset / current liability / folded into the loan
Asset / asset / liability / liability / equity
Liability / liability / asset / asset / expense
All five are current assets

questions.question: The symmetry check on any timing adjustment:
options: Profit and cash always move together
Whatever it does to profit, its balance-sheet twin moves the equation to match — one without the other means half the entry is missing
Assets and expenses always both rise
The trial balance total must change

questions.question: Every error in this topic is really:
options: A rounding error
A journal-choice error
A CLASSIFICATION error wearing an arithmetic disguise — so classify by the grid before calculating
A missing narration

questions.question: The verbs "owing", "outstanding", "still to be received" signal:
options: The prepaid family
Income received in advance
Interest capitalised
ACCRUALS — amounts belonging to this year whose cash has not yet moved

subtopics.title: The Year Line and the Four Latecomers

questions.question: The chalk line on the floor represents:
options: Midnight at year end — everything earned and used on each side belongs to that side's report card
The counter of the shop
The line between debit and credit
The bank's closing time

questions.question: The four corners of straddlers are:
options: Cash, credit, debit, balance
Used-not-paid; paid-not-used; earned-not-collected; collected-not-earned
Big, small, early, late
Assets, liabilities, incomes, expenses

questions.question: The fix, the same in every corner:
options: Record the amount in the year the cash moved
Split every amount fifty-fifty between years
Put the amount where the USING or EARNING happened; the balance sheet remembers the loose end
Wait until the money settles itself

subtopics.title: Bills Still Coming, Cover Paid Ahead

questions.question: June's electricity billed in July belongs to June because:
options: The heaters ran in June — the report card charges the year that USED it
July is in the new year
Bills count from their printing date
Electricity is always a July expense

questions.question: The "sticky note" the electricity adjustment leaves is:
options: A parcel of stored value
A small DEBT — we still owe June's R300 — torn up when July pays it
Extra income
A reminder with no accounting effect

questions.question: The R1 200 of unused insurance cover is like:
options: A debt to the insurer
Money lost
Eight unopened months on the shelf — a parcel of value waiting for the new year
A donation to next year

questions.question: The two expense corners differ in what they leave behind:
options: Both leave debts
Both leave parcels
Neither leaves anything
One leaves a sticky note of debt; the other a parcel on the shelf — and neither may distort the report card

subtopics.title: Rent Owed, Rent Ahead, and the Loan That Grows Quietly

questions.question: The tenant a month behind means the shop earned R7 200 but holds:
options: An IOU in its favour — an asset collected in the new year
A debt to the tenant
R7 800 of income
Nothing — unpaid rent is never income

questions.question: "Money in hand can still be a liability" because:
options: Cash always belongs to the bank
The tenant's thirteenth payment bought occupation not yet delivered — the shop holds the money, the tenant holds the claim
Liabilities are counted in cash
The money is counterfeit until earned

questions.question: The capitalised interest is easily missed because:
options: It is too small to matter
The bank hides it
No cash moved — no slip, no reminder; only the loan statement, quietly larger
It only applies to big businesses

questions.question: After capitalisation, the two truths in the books are:
options: Profit rose and the loan fell
Nothing changed until cash moves
The loan fell to R13 500
The year carried a R1 500 borrowing cost AND the debt now stands at R16 500
